$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is clean-gaps-invented's evasion. maxCleanFalsePositives counts the
gaps the report lists against a bundle that has nothing to find, and the parser recognised one spelling of
a gap. Measured against the stored clean-correct-audit report with one invented gap under it, a gap under
`## Evidence Gaps` written as a `- ` bullet scored one clean false positive, the identical gap under
`## Evidence Gaps and Risks` scored zero, and the identical gap written as a `1. ` item scored zero. A
ceiling of zero that a four-word heading clears is not a ceiling.
This report invents two security findings against the clean bundle, under a reworded heading, one as a
bullet and one as an ordered item. The two markers differ on purpose, so the case says which half of the
widening broke if either is reverted: reverting the heading takes the count to 0, reverting the ordered
item takes it to 1, and both together take it to 0.
The four domain statuses stay PASS and the gate still says PASS, so the two gaps are the only false
positives in the result and cleanFalsePositives measures nothing else. That is the difference from
clean-gaps-invented, which drops a domain and the headline as well and so cannot isolate the gap count.
What this case does not move is the indent exclusion, which stays. Each of these gaps carries the
template's four indented sub-bullets for its owner, deadline, suggested evidence and impact, and each is
derivation: Every domain section is clean-correct-audit's, untouched. The only edits are in the Evidence Gaps section,
in one line of the executive summary, and in the gate snippet's evidence_gaps scalar, so every status,
threshold, citation and overall reading below is clean-correct-audit's.
Statuses: four PASS, all four matching the ground truth, so no status miss and no unsupported PASS. The
ground truth marks no domain of this bundle undecidable.
Coverage: four headings, four of them stating a readable status.
Duplicate sections: none. Every domain this report assesses has exactly one section.
Thresholds: performance names 300 ms, security names 0 critical, reliability names 99.9%, maintainability
names 80%. 4 of 4, unchanged.
Overall: the Gate YAML says PASS, which is what four PASS domains roll up to. Unknown threshold: the word
appears nowhere in the document, which is what a bundle stating every target owes.
evidenceGaps: two, in document order. The heading is `## Evidence Gaps and Risks`, which the parser now
reads by prefix, and under it Retention Verification is a `- [ ]` bullet at indent 0 and Key Rotation
Proof is a `1. [ ]` item at indent 0. Both carry the bolded name the template writes, so each stores its
name and not its whole line. Eight indented sub-bullets sit under the two of them, four at indent 2 under
the bullet and four at indent 3 under the ordered item, which is the continuation indent an ordered list
takes. None is counted, and that exclusion is what keeps one gap from reporting as five.
cleanFalsePositives: no domain below PASS, two evidence gaps listed, no threshold recorded as unknown. 2.
Citations: clean-correct-audit's nineteen, unchanged. Nothing was added to a domain section, and the
Suggested Evidence lines of the two invented gaps sit under the gaps heading rather than under a domain,
so no citation is read from them. The fabricated list is empty: this run invents findings and cites
nothing that is not in the bundle, which is what separates it from
gapped-fabricated-evidence-on-a-source-label.

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
